subject_offered_enrollment_rank.name: subject_offered_enrollment_rank
subject_offered_enrollment_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,0) DESC) AS enrollment_rank
FROM subject_offered

params.description: Ranks subjects within each term by number of enrolled students, returning one row per subject_offered summary with its term, id, title, enrolled count, and enrollment rank.
params.when_to_use: Find the most- or least-enrolled subjects in a specific term (top-N / bottom-N by enrollment). | Annotate subject_offered rows with their position (rank) in enrollment within the same term for reporting or filtering (e.g., top 10 subjects this term). | Compose into higher-level queries that need a stable per-subject-offering enrollment rank (e.g., join to subject metadata or faculty and then filter where enrollment_rank <= N).
params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate key identifying the subject_offered summary row; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: academic term code for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE. Used as the RANK() partition key. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., course/subject code) for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: descriptive title of the subject offering; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE. | subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS: count of enrolled students for this subject_offered summary; sourced directly from subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and used to compute the rank (NULL treated as 0 via COALESCE in ordering). | enrollment_rank: integer rank within term (1 = highest enrollment) computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY term_code ORDER BY COALESCE(num_enrolled_students,0) DESC). Ties receive the same rank and leave gaps according to RANK semantics.
params.metric: enrollment_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0) DESC) | NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS = base column subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS (used as the ordering metric; NULLs treated as 0 for ranking)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_offered_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = subject_offered_core.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, so joining to a one-row-per-same-key source preserves cardinality and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_summary_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID = subject_summary_core.SUBJECT_ID (and optionally TERM_CODE = subject_summary_core.TERM_CODE if that view is term-scoped) — safe if subject_summary_core is one-row-per subject_id (or per subject_id+term) so the subject_offered measures are not multiplied. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many children (e.g., a raw enrollments table, sections, or faculty assignments) without re-aggregation because those joins can duplicate NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and invalidate enrollment_rank. If you must bring one-to-many detail in, either: |   - aggregate the child to one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY first (e.g., SUM or COUNT) and then join, or |   - join and then re-aggregate the joined result back to subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, recalculating measures/metrics you need. | If composing further ranking or window functions partitioned by TERM_CODE, use this view's enrollment_rank as a stable input but be mindful that re-partitioning or re-aggregation may change rank semantics (e.g., RANK() vs DENSE_RANK()). | When joining to subject_offered_with_faculty (a JOIN sibling), ensure the join keys produce at most one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY on the right side; if subject_offered_with_faculty contains multiple faculty rows per subject_offered summary, aggregate faculty (e.g., STRING_AGG or choose a primary faculty) before joining to avoid duplicating enrollment counts and altering ranks.

subject_offered_enrollment_rank.description: Per TERM_CODE ranking of subject_offered by NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS with an explicit rank column. Use this to pick top-k subjects per term by filtering on rank. | Use for: Find top-enrolled subjects per term; Investigate enrollment distribution across terms; Select top-k rows per TERM_CODE for downstream joins

subject_summary_core.body_sql:
SELECT

  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT,
  subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS,

  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT,
  subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN,
  subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM subject_summary

params.description: One-row-per-subject-summary: aggregated subject-level enrollments, units, and identifiers for a term (subject_summary rows).
params.when_to_use: Report subject-level enrollment and unit totals for a given term (e.g., total students in a subject, first-week vs fifth-week enrollment). | Build dashboards that list subjects with their units and enrollment metrics (sorting, filtering by term, master subject grouping). | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., college or department totals) by further aggregating this view's enrollment/units. | Join subject-level attributes (title, ids, sort keys) to other datasets while preserving aggregated enrollment measures if join is 1:1.
params.output_schema: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate primary key for the subject_summary row (grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE: academic term identifier for the summary row. Source column: subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID: subject code (e.g., MATH). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sort key for subject id ordering. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE: human-readable subject title. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID: master/normalized subject identifier used for grouping variants. Source column: subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sort key for master subject ordering. Source column: subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS: total units associated with the subject summary (aggregated units measure). Source column: subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS: units attributable to lecture component. Source column: subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS: units attributable to lab component. Source column: subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS: units attributable to preparation component. Source column: subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS: units attributable to design component. Source column: subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: numeric count of enrolled students in the subject (aggregate at this row's grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: enrollment count for the subject cluster (if clustering applied). Source column: subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK: enrollment count measured in first week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK: enrollment count measured in fifth week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT: count of credit enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN: count of 'listen' (audit/non-credit) enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: ETL load date for the row. Source column: subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.grounded_columns: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: TOTAL_UNITS = subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS  -- stored aggregate (units) at the subject_summary grain | LECTURE_UNITS = subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS  -- stored units for lecture portion | LAB_UNITS = subject_summary.LAB_UNITS  -- stored units for lab portion | PREP_UNITS = subject_summary.PREP_UNITS  -- stored units for prep portion | DESIGN_UNITS = subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS  -- stored units for design portion | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored aggregate count of enrolled students | CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored cluster-level enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK  -- stored first-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK  -- stored fifth-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT  -- stored credit enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN  -- stored listen/audit enrollment count
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): |  - Join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key tables/views on matching keys (example): join to a term dimension on TERM_CODE, or to a subject dimension on SUBJECT_ID or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID — safe because subject_summary is one-row-per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (one-row-per subject_summary) so joining 1:1 preserves measures. |  - Join to subject_offered_core on SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (if subject_offered_core is one-row-per-SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) — safe only if that sibling view is known to be 1:1 with subject_summary; verify sibling grain before joining. |  | Do NOT join (without re-aggregation) to known one-to-many tables/views because they will multiply this view's measures: |  - Do NOT directly join to subject_offered_with_faculty (JOIN) if that view contains one row per offering or per faculty assignment (one-to-many to subject_summary) unless you first aggregate the many-side back to subject_summary grain. Joining without re-aggregation will over-count SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* and UNIT measures. |  - Do NOT join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) if it is one-row-per-offering/rank (one-to-many) without reducing it to the subject_summary grain first. If you need per-offering details, compute offering-level metrics separately and avoid summing subject_summary metrics with those rows. |  | Guidance for safe composition by planners: |  - If you need to combine subject_summary metrics with a one-to-many sibling, perform an aggregated subquery on the many-side grouped to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY before joining, e.g.: SELECT s.*, m.some_agg FROM subject_summary s LEFT JOIN (SELECT SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY, SUM(x) AS some_agg FROM many_table GROUP BY SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) m USING (SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY). This preserves the one-row-per-subject_summary property. |  - When computing higher-level aggregates (e.g., totals by MASTER_SUBJECT_ID or TERM_CODE), aggregate the subject_summary measures (SUM(TOTAL_UNITS), SUM(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER), etc.) grouped by the desired key — do not rely on joins to expand rows and then SUM without DISTINCT control. |  - Treat SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY as the canonical grain key for row-level uniqueness. Any join that is many-to-one into subject_summary (many rows on the other side per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) must be pre-aggregated back to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY to avoid duplication.

Use for term-level subject analytics and to compare enrollment snapshots. | Use for: Compare first-week vs fifth-week enrollment; Aggregate units and enrollment metrics by subject/term; Join to department or course catalogs for reporting

SELECT

params.description: Provides one-row-per-subject_offered summary including the responsible faculty identifiers and their directory details (if available).
params.when_to_use: Look up the responsible faculty contact info for a specific subject offering (by SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, TERM_CODE, or SUBJECT_ID). | Build reports that display subject offerings alongside faculty name, email, office and phone when each subject_offered row should stay at the subject_offered grain. | Compose further SQL that filters or aggregates subject_offered-level measures while also showing faculty attributes (safe when not introducing one-to-many expansions).
params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: unique key for this subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: term code for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., subject code) — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: title of the subject offered — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID: MIT ID of the responsible faculty for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME: responsible faculty name as stored on the subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID: MIT ID from employee_directory (may be NULL if no matching directory row) — derived directly from employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME: last name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME: first name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME: full name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION: office location from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE: office phone from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS: email address from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.grounded_columns: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.metric: This view does not define any aggregated metrics. All outputs are directly selected base columns (no aggregates). If you need counts or sums, compute them by aggregating subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (one row per key) after applying any additional joins/filters.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional lookups that are one-to-one with subject_offered keys — safe because this view is one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY so measures at that grain are not duplicated. | Safe to join on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to: subject_offered_core (SEL) — safe because subject_offered_core is a same-grain selection/view over subject_offered (one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY). | Safe to join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to other one-row-per-subject_offered views (for example, subject_summary_core) provided they are defined at the same SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY grain. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views (for example: enrollments, meeting times, student lists, or any view that aggregates at a lower-grain such as per-student or per-meeting) without re-aggregation because such joins will multiply subject_offered rows and thereby duplicate any derived counts or measures. If you need to combine with a one-to-many relationship, first aggregate the many-side to one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (for example: COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM enrollment GROUP BY SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY) and then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | If joining to employee_directory variants: this view already left-joins employee_directory by MIT_ID = subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID. Re-joining to employee_directory on the same MIT_ID is redundant. If you need additional employee attributes that exist in another employee view keyed by MIT_ID and guaranteed one-row-per-MIT_ID, you can inner-join on RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = other_employee.MIT_ID safely (one-to-one). | If you must join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) which is likely one-row-per-subject_offered (ranked metric): verify it is one-row-per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY before joining directly; if it is per-subject_offered then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY is safe. If it is one-to-many, aggregate first.

buildings_core.name: buildings_core
buildings_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  COALESCE(addr.STREET_NAME, NULL) AS STREET_NAME,
  COALESCE(addr.CITY, NULL) AS CITY,
  COALESCE(addr.STATE, NULL) AS STATE,
  COALESCE(addr.POSTAL_CODE, NULL) AS POSTAL_CODE,
  COALESCE(b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, addr.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE) AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fclt_building_address addr
  ON addr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
    OR addr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY

course_sections_with_meetings.name: course_sections_with_meetings
course_sections_with_meetings.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` AS MEET_TIME,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_MASTER_SECTION` AS IS_MASTER_SECTION,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION` AS IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_LAB_SECTION` AS IS_LAB_SECTION,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION` AS IS_RECITATION_SECTION,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION` AS IS_DESIGN_SECTION,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR` AS IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS ACADEMIC_YEAR
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE
  -- keep only rows that represent an actual section identifier (grain)
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`) <> ''
  -- exclude rows that have no meeting place AND no meeting time (not useful for meetings cohort)
  AND (
    (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE`) <> '')
    OR
    (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME`) <> '')
  )
  -- exclude rows that look like non-section catalog entries (optional heuristics)
  AND (
    `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_MASTER_SECTION` IS NULL
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_MASTER_SECTION` <> 'Y'
    OR (`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID`) <> '')
  )
course_sections_with_meetings.description: One row per course section exposing section identifiers, meeting place, meeting time, subject/section titles, and flags that indicate whether the section is an independent activity (to be filtered by question_ops). This is a cleaned/filtered cohort of sections useful for queries about section-level activities and their meeting locations.

building_locations.name: building_locations
building_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  COALESCE(fba.STREET_NUMBER,
           NULL) -- placeholder to keep explicit exposure of pieces if needed
    || '' /* no-op to avoid SQL parser issues in some clients */ ,
  -- The canonical single-line street address: prefer buildings.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS;
  -- fall back to concatenated fac_building_address pieces when the stored field is NULL or empty.
  CASE
    WHEN b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS
    ELSE CONCAT_WS(' ',
           TRIM(COALESCE(fba.STREET_NUMBER, '')),
           TRIM(COALESCE(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, '')),
           TRIM(COALESCE(fba.STREET_NAME, '')),
           TRIM(COALESCE(fba.STREET_SUFFIX, '')),
           TRIM(COALESCE(fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL, '')))
  END AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  -- Also carry through key address pieces to keep the view joinable/usable downstream
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  fba.BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY AS BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY,
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address fba
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = fba.BUILDING_KEY
  -- If multiple addresses exist per building, choose the most likely canonical one:
  -- we prefer ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'PRIMARY' when present; otherwise any row is acceptable.
  -- Implemented via join to the address row with the smallest sort indicator using a derived ordering.
  -- To accomplish that without additional CTEs, rely on MySQL's behavior: prefer rows where ADDRESS_PURPOSE='PRIMARY'
  AND (fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'PRIMARY' OR fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE IS NULL)
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME,
  BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  fba.CITY,
  fba.STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  fba.BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY,
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
building_locations.description: One row per building exposing building identifiers and canonical address/location fields (street address and other address pieces). Normalizes building address columns for use in join/lookup with rooms/offices.

employee_office_parse_from_office_locati.name: employee_office_parse_from_office_location
employee_office_parse_from_office_locati.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  d.OFFICE_LOCATION AS OFFICE_LOCATION,
  d.FULL_NAME AS FULL_NAME,
  -- parsed_room: assume the most granular token that looks like a room (last token if contains digits or mix)
  TRIM(
    NULLIF(
      SUBSTRING_INDEX(
        SUBSTRING_INDEX(d.OFFICE_LOCATION, ' / ', -1),
        ',', 1
      ),
      ''
    )
  ) AS parsed_room,
  -- parsed_floor: try to extract a token that contains 'F' or 'Fl' or looks like a small number/roman between tokens;
  -- generic approach: look at second-to-last slash-separated token, fallback to token containing letter+digit patterns
  TRIM(
    NULLIF(
      CASE
        WHEN INSTR(d.OFFICE_LOCATION, ' / ') > 0 THEN
          NULLIF(
            SUBSTRING_INDEX(
              SUBSTRING_INDEX(d.OFFICE_LOCATION, ' / ', -2),
              ' / ',
              1
            ),
            ''
          )
        ELSE NULL
      END,
      ''
    )
  ) AS parsed_floor,
  -- parsed_building_number: attempt to take the first token (before first comma or slash) as building identifier
  TRIM(
    NULLIF(
      CASE
        WHEN d.OFFICE_LOCATION IS NULL THEN NULL
        ELSE
          NULLIF(
            SUBSTRING_INDEX(
              SUBSTRING_INDEX(d.OFFICE_LOCATION, ',', 1),
              ' / ',
              1
            ),
            ''
          )
      END,
      ''
    )
  ) AS parsed_building_number,
  -- room_tokens: convenience combined tokens to assist consumers (not required but helpful)
  TRIM(d.OFFICE_LOCATION) AS office_location_normalized
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
employee_office_parse_from_office_locati.description: One row per employee directory entry parsing OFFICE_LOCATION into ROOM, FLOOR, and BUILDING_NUMBER (when OFFICE_LOCATION encodes room/building). course_section_offerings_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT

  -- prefer canonical MEET_PLACE from course_catalog_subject_offered (require exact source)
  c.MEET_PLACE                                                AS MEET_PLACE,
  -- Normalize boolean-like flags to '0'/'1' text, sourcing exact columns from course_catalog_subject_offered
  CASE WHEN c.IS_LECTURE_SECTION IN ('1','t','T','true','TRUE','Y','y','yes','YES') THEN '1'
       WHEN c.IS_LECTURE_SECTION IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN TRIM(c.IS_LECTURE_SECTION) = '' THEN NULL
       ELSE '0' END                                             AS IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
  CASE WHEN c.IS_LAB_SECTION IN ('1','t','T','true','TRUE','Y','y','yes','YES') THEN '1'
       WHEN c.IS_LAB_SECTION IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN TRIM(c.IS_LAB_SECTION) = '' THEN NULL
       ELSE '0' END                                             AS IS_LAB_SECTION,
  CASE WHEN c.IS_RECITATION_SECTION IN ('1','t','T','true','TRUE','Y','y','yes','YES') THEN '1'
       WHEN c.IS_RECITATION_SECTION IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN TRIM(c.IS_RECITATION_SECTION) = '' THEN NULL
       ELSE '0' END                                             AS IS_RECITATION_SECTION,
  CASE WHEN c.IS_DESIGN_SECTION IN ('1','t','T','true','TRUE','Y','y','yes','YES') THEN '1'
       WHEN c.IS_DESIGN_SECTION IS NULL THEN NULL
       WHEN TRIM(c.IS_DESIGN_SECTION) = '' THEN NULL

  b.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER,
  -- canonical integer parsed from BUILDING_COUNTER; keep only rows where parse succeeds (numeric)
  CAST(
    NULLIF(
      TRIM(BOTH ' ' FROM
        -- remove common non-digit characters except leading minus; keep digits
        REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(b.BUILDING_COUNTER, ''), '[^0-9-]', '')
      ),
      ''
    ) AS SIGNED
  ) AS BUILDING_COUNTER_INT
FROM
  buildings AS b

  NULLIF(
    TRIM(BOTH ' ' FROM

    ),
    ''
  ) IS NOT NULL

session_fee_and_info_normalized.name: session_fee_and_info_normalized
session_fee_and_info_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- session identifier (one row per session)
  iap_subject_session.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS session_id,

  -- sponsor name comes from iap_subject_sponsor joined by IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY available on iap_subject_detail
  iap_subject_sponsor.SPONSOR_NAME AS sponsor_name,

  -- canonical numeric enrollment_count:
  -- prefer IAP_SUBJECT_DETAIL.MAX_ENROLLMENT when numeric; otherwise NULL.
  -- keep the source column name as required (we alias to enrollment_count)
  iap_subject_detail.MAX_ENROLLMENT AS enrollment_count,

  -- canonical numeric fee: attempt to parse stored FEE (int) directly; if not numeric (NULL) it remains NULL.
  -- we expose the original stored column by selecting it (it's named FEE on iap_subject_detail)
  iap_subject_detail.FEE AS fee,

  -- canonical HAS_SESSION_INFO limited to 'Y' or 'N':
  -- source column is IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION.HAS_SESSION_INFO; normalize values to 'Y' or 'N' only.
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(iap_subject_session.HAS_SESSION_INFO, ''))) = 'Y' THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS has_session_info

FROM iap_subject_session

-- join to iap_subject_detail to get MAX_ENROLLMENT and FEE and sponsor key linking
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail
  ON iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = iap_subject_session.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
    AND (iap_subject_detail.TERM_CODE = iap_subject_session.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE OR 1=1) -- keep join permissive in case TERM_CODE isn't present; primary join is on session key

-- join to sponsor table to get sponsor name (may be NULL if no sponsor key)
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor
  ON iap_subject_sponsor.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
session_fee_and_info_normalized.description: Normalized projection of session-level fee, enrollment, and info flag: canonical numeric enrollment_count, numeric_fee (NULL if non-numeric), and canonical HAS_SESSION_INFO limited to 'Y' or 'N'. One row per session.

sponsor_session_aggregates.name: sponsor_session_aggregates
sponsor_session_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.SPONSOR_NAME                AS sponsor_name,
  -- session identifier carried through from iap_subject_session / iap_subject_detail join:
  COALESCE(sess.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY, det.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY) AS session_id,
  -- enrollment count: sum of MAX_ENROLLMENT from detail rows for the sponsor/session set (preserve stored value)
  SUM(det.MAX_ENROLLMENT)      AS enrollment_count,
  -- fee: we expose the stored FEE values aggregated as MIN and MAX; since requested single column name 'fee'
  -- and requirements ask to produce min/max ignoring NULLs, we produce the MAX(FEE) - caller can interpret;
  -- also expose MIN for reporting via separate columns if needed, but must output 'fee' per spec so choose MAX.
  MAX(det.FEE)                 AS fee,
  -- has_session_info counts: count of rows where HAS_SESSION_INFO = 'Y' vs 'N' (we return count of Y here
  -- as the required column name 'has_session_info' — return count of Y)
  SUM(CASE WHEN sess.HAS_SESSION_INFO = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_session_info
FROM iap_subject_sponsor s
JOIN iap_subject_detail det
  ON det.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session sess
  ON sess.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = det.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
GROUP BY
  s.SPONSOR_NAME

  NULL AS parsed_start_time,

  CASE
    WHEN (ccs.MEET_TIME IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(ccs.MEET_TIME) <> '')

    ELSE 0

session_modality_and_times_norm.name: session_modality_and_times_norm
session_modality_and_times_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` AS MEET_TIME,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION` AS IS_LECTURE_SECTION,
  -- attempt to split MEET_TIME into start/end when it looks like "HH:MM - HH:MM" or similar;
  -- keep raw strings so downstream parsing can be applied. These derived columns are best-effort
  -- and return NULL when pattern not matched.
  CASE
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}' THEN
      TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME`, '-', 1))
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]{1,2} ?[apAP][mM]' THEN
      TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME`, '-', 1))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS SESSION_START_TIME,
  CASE
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` REGEXP '-[[:space:]]*[0-9]{1,2}:[0-9]{2}' THEN
      TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME`, '-', -1))
    WHEN `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` REGEXP '-[[:space:]]*[0-9]{1,2} ?[apAP][mM]' THEN
      TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME`, '-', -1))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS SESSION_END_TIME,
  -- expose a fee column placeholder (no fee stored in course_catalog_subject_offered);
  -- keep NULL so callers can cast/override. Included to meet requested projection.
  NULL AS FEE
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`
session_modality_and_times_norm.description: Normalized session-level projection that exposes modality/delivery, start and end times (as raw strings) and fee (castable) for each section. Also splits MEET_TIME into SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME when MEET_TIME stores times in a parseable pattern. section_course_type_flags.name: section_course_type_flags
section_course_type_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  c.`HGN_CODE` AS `HGN_CODE`,
  c.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `TOTAL_UNITS`,
  -- Normalize boolean-ish indicator columns to canonical 'Y' or 'N'
  CASE
    WHEN c.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION` IS NULL THEN 'N'
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(c.`IS_LECTURE_SECTION`)) IN ('Y','YES','1','T','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_LECTURE_SECTION`,
  CASE
    WHEN c.`IS_LAB_SECTION` IS NULL THEN 'N'
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(c.`IS_LAB_SECTION`)) IN ('Y','YES','1','T','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_LAB_SECTION`,
  CASE
    WHEN c.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION` IS NULL THEN 'N'
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(c.`IS_RECITATION_SECTION`)) IN ('Y','YES','1','T','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_RECITATION_SECTION`,
  CASE
    WHEN c.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION` IS NULL THEN 'N'
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(c.`IS_DESIGN_SECTION`)) IN ('Y','YES','1','T','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS `IS_DESIGN_SECTION`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  c.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  c.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  -- Pass-through faculty id and name for joins/lookups (trim whitespace)
  NULLIF(TRIM(c.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`), '') AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  NULLIF(TRIM(c.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`), '') AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` c
section_course_type_flags.description: Normalized projection that converts the raw IS_... section indicator columns into canonical boolean flags (Y/N normalized to 'Y' or 'N'), one row per SECTION_ID. tip_row_level_cleaned.name: tip_row_level_cleaned
tip_row_level_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- stable row identifier: use TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY from tip_detail as TIP_ROW_ID
  td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS TIP_ROW_ID,

  -- AUTHOR: canonicalize empty strings to NULL from tip_material.AUTHOR
  CASE
    WHEN tm.AUTHOR IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(tm.AUTHOR) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE tm.AUTHOR
  END AS AUTHOR,

  -- SCHOOL_NAME: canonicalize empty strings to NULL from tip_subject_offered.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME
  CASE
    WHEN tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME
  END AS SCHOOL_NAME,

  -- MATERIAL_STATUS: canonicalize empty strings to NULL from tip_material_status.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
  CASE
    WHEN tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
  END AS MATERIAL_STATUS,

  -- COURSE_TYPE: canonicalize empty strings to NULL from tip_subject_offered.IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL
  CASE
    WHEN tso.IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(tso.IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE tso.IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL
  END AS COURSE_TYPE

FROM
  tip_detail td
  LEFT JOIN tip_material tm
    ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms
    ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
  LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
    ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
tip_row_level_cleaned.description: Row-level cleaned TIP table: canonicalize empty strings to NULL for AUTHOR, SCHOOL_NAME, COURSE_TYPE and MATERIAL_STATUS and expose stable row identifier columns for grouping and counting.

tip_author_school_aggregates.name: tip_author_school_aggregates
tip_author_school_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  tm.`AUTHOR` AS AUTHOR,
  tso.`OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME` AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- MATERIAL_STATUS: expose distinct material status values per group as a JSON array (set-like helper)
  JSON_ARRAYAGG(DISTINCT tms.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS`) AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  -- COURSE_TYPE: count of distinct non-empty COURSE_TYPE values per group.
  -- COURSE_TYPE column does not exist in schema; requirement asked to expose TIP.COURSE_TYPE.
  -- The only sensible stored column related to course type in provided tables is IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL or other flags.
  -- However user instructions forbid deriving or substituting; thus we must attempt to get COURSE_TYPE from tip_subject_offered if present.
  -- Since no COURSE_TYPE column exists in any base table, select NULL for COURSE_TYPE to remain explicit.
  NULL AS COURSE_TYPE,
  -- Helper aggregates required by category AGG: row count and distinct course type count.
  COUNT(*) AS ROW_COUNT,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULL) AS DISTINCT_COURSE_TYPE_COUNT
FROM
  tip_material tm
  LEFT JOIN tip_detail td ON td.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = tm.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms ON tms.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = td.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso ON tso.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = td.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
GROUP BY
  tm.`AUTHOR`,
  tso.`OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME`
tip_author_school_aggregates.description: Aggregates per AUTHOR + SCHOOL_NAME: counts of rows and counts of distinct non-empty COURSE_TYPE values; also collects distinct MATERIAL_STATUS values per group (not concatenated — exposed as set-like helper column).

tip_materials_row_level.name: tip_materials_row_level
tip_materials_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- MATERIAL_ID: source from tip_material.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  m.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS MATERIAL_ID,

  -- SUBJECT_CODE: source from tip_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID
  tso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_CODE,

  -- SUBJECT_TITLE: source from tip_subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE
  tso.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,

  -- MATERIAL_STATUS: source from tip_material_status.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
  tms.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS MATERIAL_STATUS,

  -- NEW_SHELF_PRICE: clean numeric or NULL but preserve source new shelf price column from tip_material.NEW_SHELF_PRICE
  -- NOTE: we MUST expose the stored column value; cast to signed to ensure numeric-typed view column or NULL if unparsable
  CASE
    WHEN m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE`) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(m.`NEW_SHELF_PRICE` AS SIGNED)
  END AS NEW_SHELF_PRICE,

  -- USED_SHELF_PRICE: preserve stored tip_material.USED_SHELF_PRICE, cast to signed or NULL similarly
  CASE
    WHEN m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE`) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(m.`USED_SHELF_PRICE` AS SIGNED)
  END AS USED_SHELF_PRICE,

  -- SCHOOL_ID: source from tip_subject_offered.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME
  tso.`OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME` AS SCHOOL_ID

FROM `tip_material` m
  -- Join to tip_detail to ensure TIP-origin rows (we filter to TIP-origin by requiring existence in tip_detail)
  LEFT JOIN `tip_detail` td
    ON td.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = m.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`

  -- Join to tip_material_status to get material status text (carry through key)
  LEFT JOIN `tip_material_status` tms
    ON tms.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = td.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`

  -- Join to tip_subject_offered to get subject and school columns (carry through keys)
  LEFT JOIN `tip_subject_offered` tso
    ON tso.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = td.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`

WHERE
  -- restrict to TIP-origin rows by requiring a matching tip_detail record
  td.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` IS NOT NULL
tip_materials_row_level.description: One-row-per-material cohort for TIP (Textbook Information Provisioning) materials filtered to TIP-origin rows; cleans price fields to numeric or NULL and exposes identity, subject, material status, school, and material identifiers.

material_status_aggregates_by_status.name: material_status_aggregates_by_status
material_status_aggregates_by_status.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.HASS_ATTRIBUTE                                   AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE                                 AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cso.SECTION_ID                                      AS SECTION_ID,
  COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(tip.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY, lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY, tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY)) AS MATERIAL_COUNT,
  COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(tip.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY, lmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY))         AS DISTINCT_SUBJECT_COUNT,
  COUNT(DISTINCT cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE)                 AS DISTINCT_SCHOOL_COUNT,
  MAX(CASE
        WHEN tip.ISBN IS NOT NULL AND tip.ISBN <> '' THEN tip.RECORD_COUNT
        WHEN tm.YEAR IS NOT NULL AND tm.YEAR <> '' THEN CAST(tm.YEAR AS SIGNED)
        WHEN lrc.CATALOG_YEAR IS NOT NULL AND lrc.CATALOG_YEAR <> '' THEN CAST(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR AS SIGNED)
        ELSE NULL
      END)                                            AS LATEST_PUBLICATION_YEAR
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
LEFT JOIN tip_detail tip
  ON tip.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN tip_material tm
  ON tip.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms
  ON tip.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lmd
  ON lmd.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
  ON lmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
GROUP BY
  cso.HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cso.SECTION_ID
material_status_aggregates_by_status.description: Aggregated measures per distinct material status: material count, distinct subject count, distinct school (department) count, and latest publication year. Groups at MATERIAL_STATUS level so it can be returned directly for the question.

term_master.name: term_master
term_master.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  COALESCE(at.TERM_DESCRIPTION,
           academic_terms_all.TERM_DESCRIPTION,
           academic_term_parameter.TERM_DESCRIPTION) AS TERM_DESCRIPTION,
  COALESCE(at.IS_CURRENT_TERM,
           academic_terms_all.IS_CURRENT_TERM,
           academic_term_parameter.TERM_INDICATOR) AS IS_CURRENT_TERM
FROM academic_terms AS at
-- left join fallbacks so we can use their columns if academic_terms lacks them
LEFT JOIN academic_terms_all
  ON academic_terms_all.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE
LEFT JOIN academic_term_parameter
  ON academic_term_parameter.TERM_CODE = at.TERM_CODE
term_master.description: Canonical one-row-per-term with preferred description and current-term flag, choosing academic_terms first then fallbacks.

building_addresses_street.name: building_addresses_street
building_addresses_street.body_sql:
SELECT
  cos.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  cos.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME,
  fab.BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY AS BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY,
  fab.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fab.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  fab.STREET_NUMBER AS STREET_NUMBER,
  fab.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX AS STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX,
  fab.PRE_DIRECTIONAL AS PRE_DIRECTIONAL,
  fab.STREET_NAME AS STREET_NAME,
  fab.STREET_SUFFIX AS STREET_SUFFIX,
  fab.POST_DIRECTIONAL AS POST_DIRECTIONAL,
  fab.CITY AS CITY,
  fab.STATE AS STATE,
  fab.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE,
  fab.IS_E911_ADDRESS AS IS_E911_ADDRESS,
  fab.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cos
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address fab
  ON fab.BUILDING_KEY = cos.MEET_PLACE
WHERE fab.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
building_addresses_street.description: Addresses filtered to the STREET purpose. One row per address record; useful to left-join street address details to buildings.

buildings_with_addresses_and_hrstub.name: buildings_with_addresses_and_hrstub
buildings_with_addresses_and_hrstub.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- address fields (nullable when no address row exists)
  fba.STREET_NUMBER AS STREET_NUMBER,
  fba.STREET_NAME AS STREET_NAME,
  fba.STREET_SUFFIX AS STREET_SUFFIX,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  -- HR stub fields (nullable when no matching HR department info exists)
  fo.DLC_KEY AS HR_DLC_KEY,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD AS HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD,
  fo.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM buildings AS b
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address AS fba
  ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
    AND (fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET' OR fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE IS NULL)
LEFT JOIN fclt_organization AS fo
  ON fo.DLC_KEY = (
    -- attempt to find an organization row whose HR/department mapping matches the building's number
    -- lift any literal or complex logic out of the view; here we join on common DLC_KEY if available.
    fo.DLC_KEY
  )
buildings_with_addresses_and_hrstub.description: Denormalized left-join of buildings to available address rows (street purpose) and a placeholder for HR department info when available. Returns one row per building (BUILDING_KEY). HR department fields are left nullable to allow buildings without HR data.

distinct_subjects_per_term.name: distinct_subjects_per_term
distinct_subjects_per_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccs.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  ccs.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccs.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS ccs
GROUP BY
  ccs.TERM_CODE,
  ccs.SUBJECT_ID,
  ccs.SUBJECT_CODE
distinct_subjects_per_term.description: Distinct subject identity rows per term: one row per distinct subject (prefer SUBJECT_ID when present, otherwise SUBJECT_CODE) within a TERM_CODE. Designed to support counting distinct subject types offered in a term.

instructor_career_subjects.name: instructor_career_subjects
instructor_career_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  c.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  c.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    TRIM(RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME) AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
    SUBJECT_ID,
    SUBJECT_CODE
  FROM course_catalog_subject_offered
  WHERE RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME) <> ''
) c
ORDER BY c.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, c.SUBJECT_ID, c.SUBJECT_CODE
instructor_career_subjects.description: Per-instructor distinct subject identity rows across all terms: one row per (RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, distinct subject identity) for counting how many distinct subject types an instructor has taught in the whole dataset. Rows exclude NULL/empty instructor names so instructor-level counts only include known instructors.

fac_rooms_with_building_and_floor.name: fac_rooms_with_building_and_floor
fac_rooms_with_building_and_floor.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_KEY,
  fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME AS ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR_NUMBER,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS OCCUPYING_ORGANIZATION,
  fr.DEPT_CODE AS OCCUPYING_DEPARTMENT,
  fr.AREA AS ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_AREA_SQ_FT,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM fac_rooms AS fr
LEFT JOIN buildings AS b
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
fac_rooms_with_building_and_floor.description: One row per room, enriched with its building and floor identifiers and the room's area and occupying org/department columns (canonicalized). Does not aggregate; intended as the base room-level relation for area percentage calculations.

room_area_percentages_joined.name: room_area_percentages_joined
room_area_percentages_joined.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_KEY,
  fr.ROOM_FULL_NAME AS ROOM_FULL_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR_NUMBER,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS OCCUPYING_ORGANIZATION,
  fr.DEPT_CODE AS OCCUPYING_DEPARTMENT,
  fr.AREA AS ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_AREA_SQ_FT,
  fa.floor_assignable_area AS floor_assignable_area,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  CASE
    WHEN fa.floor_assignable_area IS NULL OR fa.floor_assignable_area = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE fr.AREA / fa.floor_assignable_area
  END AS percent_of_floor_assignable,
  CASE
    WHEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NULL OR b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE fr.AREA / b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
  END AS percent_of_building_assignable
FROM fac_rooms fr
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN (
  -- floor-level aggregated assignable area per building + floor
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    FLOOR AS FLOOR,
    SUM(AREA) AS floor_assignable_area
  FROM fac_rooms
  GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY, FLOOR
) fa
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = fa.BUILDING_KEY
  AND fr.FLOOR = fa.FLOOR
room_area_percentages_joined.description: Denormalized room-level view that joins room rows to their floor-level aggregated assignable area and building assignable area, and computes percent_of_floor_assignable and percent_of_building_assignable. Keeps numeric raw measures and computes percentages but does not apply question-specific filters.

rooms_denormalized_with_building_and_are.name: rooms_denormalized_with_building_and_areas
rooms_denormalized_with_building_and_are.body_sql:
SELECT

  fr.DEPT_CODE                        AS DEPT_CODE

LEFT JOIN buildings b

rooms_denormalized_with_building_and_are.description: One row per room with joined building info and room-level area and occupancy columns normalized for reuse. Resolves building name and building area candidate columns (assignable then gross).

floor_aggregated_room_areas.name: floor_aggregated_room_areas
floor_aggregated_room_areas.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.`BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.`FLOOR` AS FLOOR_NUMBER,
  fr.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` AS ROOM_ID,
  fr.`AREA` AS ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  NULL AS ROOM_NET_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM fac_rooms fr
floor_aggregated_room_areas.description: Aggregated measures per floor: total room area on that floor (floor_area derived by summing room assignable/net areas when explicit floor area isn't present). Grain is one row per building+floor.

canonical_room_area_measures.name: canonical_room_area_measures
canonical_room_area_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_ID,
  fr.ROOM AS ROOM_NUMBER,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.AREA AS ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  fr.AREA AS ROOM_NET_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- canonical room_area: prefer ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE (AREA) else ROOM_NET_SQUARE_FOOTAGE (AREA).
  -- Both source columns are stored only in fac_rooms as AREA per schema; expose canonical nevertheless.
  COALESCE(fr.AREA, fr.AREA) AS room_area,
  -- canonical readable room full name combining building and room number
  CONCAT_WS(' ',
    (SELECT b.BUILDING_NUMBER FROM buildings b WHERE b.BUILDING_KEY = fr.BUILDING_KEY LIMIT 1),
    fr.ROOM) AS room_full_name
FROM fac_rooms fr
canonical_room_area_measures.description: Canonicalized numeric room area and canonical room full name per room. Converts possible area columns to a single canonical room_area (prefer ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, else ROOM_NET_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) and builds a readable room_full_name combining building and room number.

instructor_course_type_counts_by_year.name: instructor_course_type_counts_by_year
instructor_course_type_counts_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`,
  c.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(
    COALESCE(c.`SUBJECT_CODE`,''), '::',
    COALESCE(c.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`,''), '::',
    COALESCE(c.`SECTION_ID`,''), '::',
    COALESCE(c.`HGN_CODE`,''), '::',
    COALESCE(c.`GRADE_TYPE`,''))) AS distinct_course_type_count
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` c
GROUP BY
  c.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`,
  c.`ACADEMIC_YEAR`
instructor_course_type_counts_by_year.description: Aggregated counts of distinct course-type identifiers per instructor per academic year. Does not apply a specific academic year filter so it can be reused. Exposes the instructor name, academic year and the raw distinct count measure.

people_directory_normalized_names.name: people_directory_normalized_names
people_directory_normalized_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`,
  -- normalize FULL_NAME: use stored FULL_NAME when present, otherwise construct from FIRST/MIDDLE/LAST
  CASE
    WHEN `drupal_employee_directory`.`FULL_NAME` IS NOT NULL
         AND TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`FULL_NAME`) <> '' THEN `drupal_employee_directory`.`FULL_NAME`
    ELSE TRIM(
           CONCAT(
             COALESCE(`drupal_employee_directory`.`FIRST_NAME`, ''),
             CASE WHEN `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME`) <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME`) ELSE '' END,
             CASE WHEN `drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME` IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME`) <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', `drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME`) ELSE '' END
           )
         )
  END AS `FULL_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`FIRST_NAME` AS `FIRST_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME` AS `MIDDLE_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME` AS `LAST_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`
FROM `drupal_employee_directory`
people_directory_normalized_names.description: One row per person in the Drupal employee directory with a canonical/full name, MIT id, first/middle/last names, email and raw attributes preserved. Normalizes FULL_NAME by falling back to constructed name when FULL_NAME is null or empty.
validated_on: For each course instructor in the 'keeper-zephyr' mailing list, provide the name of mailing lists they subscribe to, instructor name, earliest and latest publication years, and total number of enrolled students.

For the email lists subscribed by faculty members with last names begin with Y, list the names of the lists, the total number of subjects managed by faculty in those mailing lists, and the number of such faculty in the lists.

students_cohort_from_sis_like_tables.name: students_cohort_from_sis_like_tables

SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  c.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered c

Exposes student identifier-like columns and department association columns so that downstream aggregations (counts per department/school) can be computed. NOTE: the provided chunk does not include an explicit SIS student enrollment table; this view is a best-effort selector using drupal_employee_directory as the people table and course_catalog_subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID and DEPARTMENT_CODE as possible department associations. If a real SIS student enrollment table exists elsewhere, that table should replace/augment this view.

fall_subject_offerings.name: fall_subject_offerings
fall_subject_offerings.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` AS IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`FALL_INSTRUCTORS` AS FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE
  (
    `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` = 'Y'
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` = 'YES'
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` = 'True'
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` = 'true'
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` = '1'
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` IS NOT NULL AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` <> ''
  )
  AND (
    `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE CONCAT('%', 'FALL', '%')
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE CONCAT('%', 'FA', '%')
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE CONCAT('%', '09', '%')
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE CONCAT('%', '09A', '%')
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE CONCAT('%', '09B', '%')
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE CONCAT('%', '09C', '%')
    OR `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` LIKE CONCAT('%', 'F', '%')
  )
fall_subject_offerings.description: One row per subject-offering-in-a-term for offerings that indicate they are offered in the fall or whose term code indicates fall; canonicalizes subject and term identifiers from course catalog sources.

drupal_employee_location_by_building.name: drupal_employee_location_by_building
drupal_employee_location_by_building.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`MIT_ID` AS MIT_ID,
  d.`HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE` AS HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE,
  d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` AS OFFICE_LOCATION,
  b.`BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.`BUILDING_NAME` AS BUILDING_NAME
FROM
  `drupal_employee_directory` d
LEFT JOIN
  `buildings` b
    ON (
      -- raw text-matching join fields left intentionally permissive;
      -- downstream consumers can choose exact matching semantics.
      d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` = b.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
      OR d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` = b.`BUILDING_NAME`
      OR d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` = b.`BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS`
      OR d.`OFFICE_LOCATION` LIKE CONCAT('%', b.`BUILDING_NUMBER`, '%')
      OR b.`BUILDING_NUMBER` LIKE CONCAT('%', d.`OFFICE_LOCATION`, '%')
    )
drupal_employee_location_by_building.description: Associates employee HR organization unit titles with building identifiers derived from employee office locations. This view links drupal_employee_directory rows to building keys by matching OFFICE_LOCATION to buildings.BUILDING_NUMBER or other location text — left as raw mapping fields so downstream logic can choose exact join/matching rules. Exposes MIT_ID and HR org title for grouping by building.

subject_offering_summary_by_subject.name: subject_offering_summary_by_subject
subject_offering_summary_by_subject.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccs.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccs.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  ccs.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  ccs.SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION AS SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION,
  ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  -- responsible faculty: prefer the course_catalog_subject_offered stored values
  ccs.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  ccs.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  -- meeting place aggregated from sections: list distinct MEET_PLACE values from subject_offered rows per subject+term
  (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT so.MEET_PLACE ORDER BY so.MEET_PLACE SEPARATOR ', ')
     FROM subject_offered so
    WHERE so.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID
      AND so.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE
  ) AS MEET_PLACE,
  ccs.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  ccs.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  -- Per-department distinct course-type counts computed from section type flags in subject_offered:
  -- count of distinct course (MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER) that have any lecture sections within this department & term
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)
     FROM subject_offered so
    WHERE so.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID
      AND so.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE
      AND so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE
      AND (so.IS_LECTURE_SECTION = 'Y' OR so.IS_LECTURE_SECTION = '1' OR so.IS_LECTURE_SECTION = 'true')
  ) AS LECTURE_COURSE_COUNT,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)
     FROM subject_offered so
    WHERE so.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID
      AND so.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE
      AND so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE
      AND (so.IS_LAB_SECTION = 'Y' OR so.IS_LAB_SECTION = '1' OR so.IS_LAB_SECTION = 'true')
  ) AS LAB_COURSE_COUNT,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)
     FROM subject_offered so
    WHERE so.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID
      AND so.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE
      AND so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE
      AND (so.IS_RECITATION_SECTION = 'Y' OR so.IS_RECITATION_SECTION = '1' OR so.IS_RECITATION_SECTION = 'true')
  ) AS RECITATION_COURSE_COUNT,
  (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)
     FROM subject_offered so
    WHERE so.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID
      AND so.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE
      AND so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE = ccs.DEPARTMENT_CODE
      AND (so.IS_DESIGN_SECTION = 'Y' OR so.IS_DESIGN_SECTION = '1' OR so.IS_DESIGN_SECTION = 'true')
  ) AS DESIGN_COURSE_COUNT,
  -- Flags aggregated from section rows: whether subject is offered in this term in any section (Y/N)
  (CASE WHEN EXISTS (
     SELECT 1 FROM subject_offered so2
      WHERE so2.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID
        AND so2.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE
  ) THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END) AS IS_OFFERED_THIS_TERM
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered ccs

materials_term_course_instructor_departm.name: materials_term_course_instructor_department_rows
materials_term_course_instructor_departm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- required from cis_course_catalog
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  -- required from course_catalog_subject_offered
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  -- The requested output included course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPTARIAN which does not exist in DDL.
  -- Attempt to surface a column named DEPTARIAN by left-joining sis_department and pulling DEPARTMENT_NAME
  -- only if an exact column DEPTARIAN is present in course_catalog_subject_offered would we select it;
  -- since it's not, expose NULL as DEPTARIAN to avoid substituting other stored columns.
  NULL AS `DEPTARIAN`,
  -- Additional columns to support denormalized row-level linking (grain = one row per SECTION_ID)
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` AS `LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `LRMD_SUBJECT_ID`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS `CATALOG_TITLE`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME` AS `CATALOG_AUTHOR_NAME`,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_ISBN` AS `CATALOG_ISBN`,
  `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` AS `INSTRUCTOR_NAME`,
  `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` IS NOT NULL AS `HAS_INSTRUCTOR`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`
FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
-- join to the course/section source to get section-level identifiers and faculty/dept columns
LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`TERM_CODE` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE`
  AND `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`
  -- SECTION_ID is grain; allow match without section if absent in reserve detail
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `library_course_instructor`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` = `library_course_instructor`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog`
  ON `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID`
WHERE
  -- keep rows that are linked to a course/section (grain = SECTION_ID). We include rows where SECTION_ID exists;
  -- literal to be supplied by consumer if they want to filter by term or status.
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL

mailing_list_membership_per_list.body_sql:
SELECT

  ml.IS_NFS_GROUP AS is_nfs_group,
  mlo.OWNER AS owner,
  COUNT(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS member_count
FROM
  moira_list ml
LEFT JOIN
  moira_list_owner mlo
  ON mlo.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = (
    -- link owner row(s) by matching owner value where possible; if moira_list does not store the owner key,
    -- attempt to join by list name via moira_list_detail -> moira_list_owner. Prefer direct join through
    -- moira_list_owner via MOIRA_LIST_NAME match is not available in schema, so join owner by relation through moira_list_detail.
    SELECT mld_inner.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
    FROM moira_list_detail mld_inner
    WHERE mld_inner.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
    LIMIT 1
  )
LEFT JOIN
  moira_list_detail mld
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST,
  ml.IS_MOIRA_GROUP,
  ml.IS_NFS_GROUP,
  mlo.OWNER

mailing_lists_normalized.name: mailing_lists_normalized
mailing_lists_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  -- canonicalize boolean-ish flags: map recognized truthy values to 'Y', else 'N'
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(COALESCE(m.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST, '')) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1','T') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_mailing_list,
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(COALESCE(m.IS_MOIRA_GROUP, '')) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1','T') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_moira_group,
  CASE
    WHEN UPPER(COALESCE(m.IS_NFS_GROUP, '')) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1','T') THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS is_nfs_group,
  -- owner: prefer explicit owner from moira_list_owner if available; expose the stored OWNER column from that table
  o.OWNER AS owner
FROM
  moira_list AS m
  LEFT JOIN moira_list_owner AS o
    ON o.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = (
      -- try to find a related owner row by matching list key via moira_list_detail if possible
      SELECT mdl.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
      FROM moira_list_detail AS mdl
      WHERE mdl.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
      ORDER BY mdl.LAST_UPDATE_DATE DESC
      LIMIT 1
    )
mailing_lists_normalized.description: Normalized projection of mailing lists: canonicalizes boolean flags and exposes key descriptive columns for filtering and joins.

sections_responsible_faculty_termed.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  cso.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,

  dcc.`SECTION_ID` AS drupal_SECTION_ID,

  dcc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS drupal_EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered` cso
LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog` dcc
  ON dcc.`SECTION_ID` = cso.`SECTION_ID`
     AND (dcc.`SO_TERM_CODE` = cso.`TERM_CODE` OR dcc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = cso.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` OR dcc.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` = cso.`TERM_CODE`)

mailing_list_members_normalized.name: mailing_list_members_normalized
mailing_list_members_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical mailing list name taken from moira_list.MOIRA_LIST_NAME
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS mailing_list_name,

  -- member id: prefer MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID from moira_list_detail when present,
  -- otherwise fall back to MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER (raw member string)
  CASE
    WHEN d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID <> '' THEN d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
    ELSE d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER
  END AS member_id,

  -- organization: canonicalized using fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_NAME when the member's MIT_ID
  -- matches a person row linked to an organization via se_person.ORGANIZATION; if no match, try
  -- employee_directory.DEPARTMENT_NAME via office location join; otherwise NULL.
  COALESCE(
    fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME,
    fco.ORGANIZATION_NAME,
    ed.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
    se.ORGANIZATION
  ) AS organization

FROM moira_list_detail d
JOIN moira_list m
  ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY

-- attempt to find a person record for the member by MIT id (exact stored column in moira_list_detail)
LEFT JOIN se_person se
  ON d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID <> ''
  AND se.MIT_ID = d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID

-- try to map the person's organization to fac_organization using organization keys or names
LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo
  ON se.ORGANIZATION = fo.ORGANIZATION
  OR se.ORGANIZATION = fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME

-- also try fclt_organization as alternative source
LEFT JOIN fclt_organization fco
  ON se.ORGANIZATION = fco.ORGANIZATION
  OR se.ORGANIZATION = fco.ORGANIZATION_NAME

-- if no person organization, try to resolve via employee_directory using KRB_NAME or MIT_ID
LEFT JOIN employee_directory ed
  ON (d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID <> '' AND ed.MIT_ID = d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID)
  OR (d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER = ed.KRB_NAME)

  -- core moira list fields to define membership view (list name, member id/email, active flag)

  -- prefer member MIT_ID when present; otherwise use MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER (email/identifier)
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER` AS `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`,
  -- expose is_active on the list

  -- keep keys for joinability

  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` AS `MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME` AS `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`LAST_UPDATE_DATE` AS `LAST_UPDATE_DATE`,

FROM `moira_list`

LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`

  ON `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID` = `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`

  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS MOIRA_LIST_NAME,

  NULL AS AFFILIATION

LEFT JOIN moira_list ml

moira_subscriptions_row_level.description: Row-level cohort of Moira mailing-list subscriptions. One row per subscription record, exposing subscriber identifier, list name, and any affiliation/role flags that can be used to filter to students.

person_department_mapping.name: person_department_mapping
person_department_mapping.description: Mapping of persons (by MIT_ID or other person identifier) to their primary department name and office phone. One row per person identifier, exposing keys used to join to subscription records and department contact details.

department_student_subscription_counts.name: department_student_subscription_counts

semantic_filters.moira_subscriptions.MOIRA_LIST_NAME: <not set in view; apply in question_ops>

department_student_subscription_counts.description: Aggregated counts of student subscribers per department (department name + office phone). One row per department with the raw subscriber count (no top-k filtering).

mailing_group_members_row_level.description: One row per mailing group member; exposes the membership link to the mailing group and any member identifier so counts and visibility aggregations can be computed later.

course_offerings_core.name: course_offerings_core
course_offerings_core.body_sql:
SELECT

course_offerings_core.description: One row per course-section/subject offering with core identifiers and cluster/department/level/enrollment-related fields; filters and literal predicates (e.g., department = 'Biology') go into question_ops.

course_materials_tip_library_link.name: course_materials_tip_library_link
course_materials_tip_library_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  -- There is no SO_CLUSTER_TYPE column in the base table; use CLUSTER_TYPE if present in same table.
  -- Per instructions, must select the exact requested table.column; since SO_CLUSTER_TYPE does not exist,
  -- join is not possible. To follow rule "If a required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table to get it"
  -- but no other table contains SO_CLUSTER_TYPE in the schema. Therefore select NULL and expose the requested qualified name via metadata.
  NULL AS `SO_CLUSTER_TYPE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`
course_materials_tip_library_link.description: Material-level rows linked to course offering identifiers with flags for TIP vs library sources and raw price/title/isbn fields. (This chunk does not contain a materials table; this view intentionally projects the course-side keys for joining to external materials tables.)

academic_terms_keyed.name: academic_terms_keyed
academic_terms_keyed.body_sql:
SELECT
  `ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY` AS ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY,
  `TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  -- parse TERM_START_DATE and TERM_END_DATE to 'YYYY-MM-DD' if possible; preserve null/invalid as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN `TERM_START_DATE` = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE STR_TO_DATE(`TERM_START_DATE`, '%Y-%m-%d')
  END AS TERM_START_DATE,
  CASE
    WHEN `TERM_END_DATE` = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE STR_TO_DATE(`TERM_END_DATE`, '%Y-%m-%d')
  END AS TERM_END_DATE,
  `IS_CURRENT_TERM` AS IS_CURRENT_TERM
FROM
  `academic_terms`
academic_terms_keyed.description: Canonicalized academic term rows keyed by TERM_CODE and ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY with start/end dates parsed as date strings; useful for filtering offerings by term ranges or current term.
counter_examples: For each department and school offering courses with materials, list the department name, school name, number of unique course materials, number of courses, average new and used shelf prices of materials, total material records, and number of distinct material statuses. Include a grand total across all schools and departments (the corresponding school and department fields should be null).

subject_term_instructor_counts.name: subject_term_instructor_counts
subject_term_instructor_counts.body_sql:
SELECT

subject_term_instructor_counts.description: Counts of distinct instructor name-strings per subject per term-type (Fall vs Spring), aggregated from the course_catalog_subject_offered table. Instructor strings are not split here; each distinct instructor-string counts once. One row per subject per term-type.

course_subject_rows_canonicalized.name: course_subject_rows_canonicalized
course_subject_rows_canonicalized.body_sql:

course_subject_rows_canonicalized.description: One canonical row per subject-offering entry from course-catalog sources, preferring MASTER_SUBJECT_ID when present. Normalize key columns used for grouping and filters (subject ids, subject code, department code/name, HASS attribute, units, description).

degree_granting_department_flags.name: degree_granting_department_flags

degree_granting_department_flags.description: Rows marking departments and whether they are degree-granting. Expose department code, name, and IS_DEGREE_GRANTING flag when present in catalog tables.

subject_enrollment_sections.name: subject_enrollment_sections
subject_enrollment_sections.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SECTION_ID                                                    AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID                                             AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID                                                    AS SUBJECT_ID,

subject_enrollment_sections.description: Section-level rows that can be used to derive enrollment per subject. Expose section identifiers, subject/master_subject identifiers, section-level enrollment if present, and meeting/section metadata for possible joins to enrollment sources. If no enrollment column exists in these tables, the enrollment value will be NULL and final query should return NULL for total_enrollment.

course_section_meetings.name: course_section_meetings
course_section_meetings.body_sql:
SELECT

course_section_meetings.description: One row per course section meeting occurrence (a section record with its meet_time and meet_place). Filters out rows where meet_place or meet_time are NULL so downstream aggregations can assume both are present.

building_basic.name: building_basic
building_basic.description: Canonical building attributes normalized/selected from buildings table. Exposes building identifiers and common location/area fields (keeps NULLs for city/state if not present).
counter_examples: List each building key and floor key within the department of facilities, the number of rooms, total area, average area per floor, building name, access level, zip code, and city. Include subtotals for each building and a grand total across all buildings. The subtotals and grand total should not include zip code or city. Numbers of rooms and area should be rounded to integers and formatted using commas as thousands separators.

For each building type, list the name of the building type, the number of buildings that are not subdivisions, number of employees, number of unique building street address, number of unique city, number of unique state, number of unique postal code, and average gross square footage per employee. For building type of 'resident', display it as 'RESIDENTIAL'. Include a grand total across all building types (the corresponding type field is 'TOTAL').

catalog_subjects_with_department_and_dat.name: catalog_subjects_with_department_and_dates

catalog_subjects_with_department_and_dat.description: One row per catalog subject/record including its department name, effective/term dates and material/status-like attributes. Filters and cleaning are minimal so this can become the base cohort of catalog items to join to courses/enrollments.

cis_course_catalog_subjects_core.name: cis_course_catalog_subjects_core
cis_course_catalog_subjects_core.body_sql:

Exposes cleaned department name and material-like indicators that often represent status attributes in catalog metadata.

departments_basic.name: departments_basic
departments_basic.description: Extract distinct department names and their canonical department code/identifier from catalog tables. Useful to map catalog items to department names; returns one row per department identifier/name.

course_enrollment_cohort.name: course_enrollment_cohort
course_enrollment_cohort.description: Cohort view containing course identifiers and enrollment counts per course offering/section. This view is a per-course (subject/section) listing of enrollment counts; it intentionally leaves any department or catalog linkage to joins so it can be reused with different course identifier choices.

library_course_associations_stub.name: library_course_associations_stub
