semantic_filters.course_catalog_subject_offered.MASTER_SU: IS NOT NULL OR course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL

library_course_associations_stub.description: Placeholder/cohort view exposing the stable course identifiers used to associate courses with library catalog items. This chunk does not contain library tables, so this view lists the course-side join keys that downstream joins should use to link to library associations (one row per course identifier).

course_offered_by_department_school.name: course_offered_by_department_school
course_offered_by_department_school.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccs.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccs.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  ccs.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME AS OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,
  tso.IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL AS IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL,
  ccs.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS ccs
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered AS tso
  ON tso.TERM_CODE = ccs.TERM_CODE
  AND tso.SUBJECT_ID = ccs.SUBJECT_ID
  AND tso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = ccs.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
WHERE tso.IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL = 'N'
course_offered_by_department_school.description: Cohort of offered courses (sections/subjects) that exposes canonical grouping keys: school name (if available), department name, course/subject identifiers and term. Filters out offerings that indicate 'no course material' (IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL = 'N') to match questions about courses that have materials.

tip_material_rowlevel.name: tip_material_rowlevel
tip_material_rowlevel.body_sql:
SELECT
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY        AS MATERIAL_ID,
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS    AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS  AS STUDENT_ENROLLMENT
FROM tip_material AS tm
LEFT JOIN tip_detail AS td
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status AS tms
  ON tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered AS tso
  ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
-- view_filters: keep only rows that are TIP materials (lift literals out of view)
tip_material_rowlevel.description: Row-level cohort of TIP (Teaching and Learning Initiative) material records. Include the material identifier, material status, and student enrollment per record. This view is a straightforward subset selecting records that are TIP materials (filter left in view_filters) but otherwise exposes raw columns to allow counts, sums, and distinct counts downstream.

tip_materials_status_canonical.name: tip_materials_status_canonical
tip_materials_status_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS MATERIAL_ID,
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  CAST(
    NULLIF(
      COALESCE(
        tso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
        lso.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
        NULL
      ),
      ''
    ) AS SIGNED
  ) AS STUDENT_ENROLLMENT
FROM tip_detail td
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
  ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lso
  ON td.SUBJECT_ID = lso.SUBJECT_ID
tip_materials_status_canonical.description: Normalized projection of TIP material status values and canonicalized student enrollment numeric value. Exposes canonical MATERIAL_STATUS (NULLs preserved for downstream choice to label), numeric STUDENT_ENROLLMENT (cast/coalesced to numeric) and MATERIAL_ID. Useful for grouping, deduping, and numeric aggregations.

tip_materials_by_status_aggregate.name: tip_materials_by_status_aggregate
tip_materials_by_status_aggregate.body_sql:
SELECT
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS        AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  COUNT(DISTINCT tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS MATERIAL_ID,
  SUM(IFNULL(so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,0)) AS STUDENT_ENROLLMENT
FROM tip_material_status AS tms
LEFT JOIN tip_detail AS td
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_material AS tm
  ON tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered AS so
  ON so.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
GROUP BY
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
tip_materials_by_status_aggregate.description: Pre-aggregated metrics of TIP materials grouped by MATERIAL_STATUS: distinct material count, record count, and total student enrollment. Produces one row per MATERIAL_STATUS (NULL preserved). This AGG view provides the exact grouped metrics the question requests except for the required 'Grand Total' row which should be appended by the final query (or computed by an outer rollup).

academic_terms_cohort.name: academic_terms_cohort
academic_terms_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY` AS `ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY`,

academic_terms_cohort.description: One row per term (row-level cohort) from the primary academic terms table, normalized for missing values. Exposes keys and grouping dimensions used in downstream grouping and joins to term parameters.

academic_term_parameter_by_term.name: academic_term_parameter_by_term
academic_term_parameter_by_term.description: One row per academic_term_parameter entry exposing TERM_CODE and TERM_PARAMETER for counting distinct department-level term parameters for terms. Keeps raw TERM_PARAMETER values for de-duplication and joins.

buildings_core_norm.name: buildings_core_norm
buildings_core_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
  -- preserve stored integers for gross and assignable sqft from buildings table
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM
  buildings b
-- Only include one row per BUILDING_KEY (buildings table is already at building grain).
-- Filter out rows missing BUILDING_NAME or CAMPUS_SECTOR when used by downstream queries;
-- here we apply a conservative filter to exclude clearly empty/NULL BUILDING_NAME.
WHERE
  b.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND b.BUILDING_KEY <> ''
  AND b.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL
  AND b.BUILDING_NAME <> ''
buildings_core_norm.description: Normalized/cleaned building-level rows with canonical numeric casts for floors, assignable area, and rooms. One row per building (BUILDING_KEY). Filters out rows missing BUILDING_NAME or CAMPUS_SECTOR when used (filtering for NULL/empty left to question_ops).
counter_examples: Calculate the total assignable and non-assignable area for each building by summing up the respective areas of all its floors. For each building, list the building name, building number, total assignable area, total non-assignable area, and total room count, sorted in descending order of the total assignable area.

List the name, number, construction date, and type of all buildings, along with the count of addresses associated with each building, the average gross area of the buildings, and the total number of rooms in each building. Sort the results by building name.

building_sector_link_join.name: building_sector_link_join
building_sector_link_join.body_sql:

FROM

building_sector_link_join.description: Denormalized view linking building rows to their campus sector and basic geographic/ownership attributes. Grain is one row per building (BUILDING_KEY). Exposes CAMPUS_SECTOR and location/ownership columns needed for sector grouping and output. (If campus sector is stored in a different table in other chunks, that join would be added; in this chunk we expose building identifiers for such joins.)

sector_totals_agg.name: sector_totals_agg
sector_totals_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  fb.CAMPUS_SECTOR AS CAMPUS_SECTOR
FROM
  buildings b
JOIN
  fac_building fb
    ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
sector_totals_agg.description: Aggregated totals per campus sector: sums of numeric building measures (TOTAL_FLOORS and TOTAL_ASSIGNABLE_AREA equivalents) and counts of buildings. Grain is one row per campus sector (CAMPUS_SECTOR). This view expects to be fed denormalized rows that include CAMPUS_SECTOR and numeric measures per building; since CAMPUS_SECTOR is not stored in the buildings table in this chunk, the final query will join and supply that column before grouping.

course_catalog_section_instructors.name: course_catalog_section_instructors
course_catalog_section_instructors.body_sql:

SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- Room-level unique identifier: prefer fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY when available,
  -- fallback to fclt_rooms.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, then fclt_rooms_hist.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, then space_detail.SPACE_UNIT_KEY
  COALESCE(fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY, frt.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, frth.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, sd.SPACE_UNIT_KEY) AS ROOM_ID,
  -- Organization identifier: prefer room-level organization keys from fac_rooms or fclt_rooms variants,
  -- else use fclt_organization_hist.ORGANIZATION_ID if available, else NULL
  COALESCE(fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY, frt.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY, frth.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY, fo.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS ORGANIZATION_ID
FROM buildings b
-- left join facility rooms (operational current rooms)
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
-- left join facilities rooms current (alternate naming)
LEFT JOIN fclt_rooms frt
  ON frt.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_NUMBER OR frt.BUILDING_ROOM = fr.SPACE_ID
-- historical facility rooms by fiscal period
LEFT JOIN fclt_rooms_hist frth
  ON frth.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_NUMBER AND frth.SPACE_ID IS NOT NULL
-- space_detail to capture rooms defined in space_detail table
LEFT JOIN space_detail sd
  ON sd.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
-- fclt_organization_hist to surface organization identifiers when present
LEFT JOIN fclt_organization_hist fo
  ON fo.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY = COALESCE(fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY, frt.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, frth.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, sd.SPACE_UNIT_KEY)
rooms_by_building_with_org.description: One row per room (room-level) linking room -> building -> organization identifier. iap_sessions_by_category_agg.name: iap_sessions_by_category_agg
iap_sessions_by_category_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS CATEGORY_ID,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY) AS NUM_UNIQUE_SESSIONS,
  SUM(d.ATTENDANCE + 0) AS TOTAL_ATTENDEES,
  MIN(d.TERM_CODE) AS MIN_TERM_CODE,
  MAX(d.TERM_CODE) AS MAX_TERM_CODE,
  -- most common sponsor name per category: pick sponsor with highest count; break ties by sponsor key
  (SELECT ss.SPONSOR_NAME
   FROM iap_subject_sponsor ss
   JOIN iap_subject_detail dd ON ss.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = dd.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
   WHERE dd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
   GROUP BY ss.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY, ss.SPONSOR_NAME
   ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, ss.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
   LIMIT 1) AS MOST_COMMON_SPONSOR,
  -- most common session start time per category from iap_subject_session.SESSION_START_TIME
  (SELECT s2.SESSION_START_TIME
   FROM iap_subject_session s2
   JOIN iap_subject_detail dd2 ON s2.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = dd2.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
   WHERE dd2.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
   GROUP BY s2.SESSION_START_TIME
   ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, s2.SESSION_START_TIME
   LIMIT 1) AS MOST_COMMON_START_TIME
FROM iap_subject_category c
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_session s
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
GROUP BY c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
iap_sessions_by_category_agg.description: Aggregate measures per IAP category: counts of distinct sessions, sum of attendee counts, min and max TERM_CODE, most frequent sponsor and most frequent start time. Built from the session-level view.

SELECT
  fo.D_CODE AS BREAK_GROUP,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS ORGANIZATION_ID,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  -- Build a formatted name but source ORGANIZATION (name) must come from fac_organization; include ORGANIZATION_NUMBER and ORGANIZATION to allow deterministic formatting
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(fo.ORGANIZATION, ''),
    CASE WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER <> '' THEN CONCAT(' (', fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER, ')') ELSE '' END
  ) AS FORMATTED_NAME,
  hf.EMERITUS_STATUS AS EMERITUS_STATUS,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AS ORGANIZATION_NUMBER,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL AS LEVEL,
  md.HIERARCHY_TYPE AS HIERARCHY_TYPE,
  fp.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID
FROM fac_organization fo
-- join organization <-> dlc mapping to reach master_dept_hierarchy which contains hierarchy type
LEFT JOIN fclt_org_dlc_key odk
  ON odk.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY = fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY
LEFT JOIN master_dept_hierarchy md
  ON md.DLC_KEY = odk.DLC_KEY
-- join faculty roster to obtain EMERITUS_STATUS; match on HR_ORG_UNIT_ID or ORGANIZATION_NAME if roster key is HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE per schema note
LEFT JOIN hr_faculty_roster hf
  ON hf.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE = fo.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID OR hf.DIRECTORY_ORG_UNIT_TITLE = fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME
-- join person/employer table for MIT_ID rows; use opa_person_current and employee_directory and warehouse_users as possible person sources,
-- but requirement says fac_person.MIT_ID in output columns; there is no fac_person table — use available person sources and carry MIT_ID from them.
LEFT JOIN opa_person_current fp
  ON fp.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID = fo.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID
LEFT JOIN employee_directory ed
  ON ed.OFFICE_LOCATION = fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AND fp.MIT_ID IS NULL
LEFT JOIN warehouse_users wu
  ON wu.UNIT_ID = fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AND fp.MIT_ID IS NULL AND ed.MIT_ID IS NULL
-- If multiple person sources join produce rows for each matching MIT_ID; union-like multiplicity achieved via COALESCE in select is avoided to keep grain; instead expose fp.MIT_ID (primary)

One row per employer (employee) assignment to an organization, exposing keys and attributes needed for grouping and filtering by organization, level, hierarchy type, emeritus status, and formatted name construction.

organization_canonical_attributes.name: organization_canonical_attributes
organization_canonical_attributes.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS ORGANIZATION_ID,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORGANIZATION_NAME,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AS ORGANIZATION_NUMBER,
  -- Canonicalize level: prefer ORGANIZATION_LEVEL, fall back to NULL; trim and upper
  NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL)), '') AS LEVEL,
  -- HIERARCHY_TYPE: canonicalize common variants (normalize to upper trimmed)
  NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(fo.D_CODE)), '') AS HIERARCHY_TYPE,
  -- BREAK_GROUP: preserve if present on fac_organization (not in schema => expose NULL)
  NULL AS BREAK_GROUP,
  -- EMERITUS_STATUS: not stored on fac_organization; expose NULL to keep canonical schema
  NULL AS EMERITUS_STATUS,
  -- FORMATTED_NAME: assemble reusable template pieces based on canonicalized LEVEL.
  -- We produce a single FORMATTED_NAME string that encodes level_based_prefix and level_based_suffix
  -- as "prefix|||suffix" so downstream queries can split. Prefix/suffix chosen by common org levels.
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL)) IN ('SCHOOL','SCHOOL/UNIT','COLLEGE') THEN
      CONCAT(
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER), ''),''),
        CASE WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER),''),'') <> '' THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME), ''),''),
        '|||', -- separator between prefix and suffix
        '' -- suffix empty for school-level (name placed after number)
      )
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL)) IN ('DEPARTMENT','DEPT','DIVISION') THEN
      CONCAT(
        '', -- prefix empty for department-level
        '|||',
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME), ''),'')
      )
    WHEN TRIM(UPPER(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL)) IN ('LAB','CENTER','INSTITUTE') THEN
      CONCAT(
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME),''),''),
        '|||',
        '' 
      )
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(UPPER(fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL)), '') IS NULL THEN
      -- When level unknown, provide ORGANIZATION_NAME as prefix to maximize usability
      CONCAT(
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME),''),''),
        '|||',
        ''
      )
    ELSE
      -- Default assembly: number followed by name as prefix, empty suffix
      CONCAT(
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER),''),''),
        CASE WHEN COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER),''),'') <> '' AND COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME),''),'') <> '' THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
        COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME),''),''),
        '|||',
        ''
      )
  END AS FORMATTED_NAME
FROM fac_organization fo
organization_canonical_attributes.description: Canonicalized organization attributes and formatted name pieces. Normalize nulls, trim/canonicalize level and hierarchy type values, and produce a FORMATTED_NAME template columns (level_based_prefix, level_based_suffix) so final queries can assemble names according to organization level rules.

buildings_address_counts.name: buildings_address_counts
buildings_address_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  COALESCE(fba.addr_count, 0) 
    + COALESCE(fcltba.addr_count, 0) 
    + COALESCE(facba.addr_count, 0) AS total_address_count,
  -- breakouts by table (counts of address rows matched by BUILDING_KEY or BUILDING_NUMBER)
  COALESCE(fba.addr_count, 0) AS fclt_building_address_count,
  COALESCE(fcltba.addr_count, 0) AS fac_building_address_count,
  COALESCE(facba.addr_count, 0) AS fac_building_addr_alt_count
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN (
  -- counts from fclt_building_address matched by BUILDING_KEY or BUILDING_NUMBER
  SELECT
    FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
    COUNT(*) AS addr_count
  FROM fclt_building_address
  GROUP BY FCLT_BUILDING_KEY

  UNION ALL

  -- also include rows keyed by BUILDING_NUMBER: they'll be aggregated up to BUILDING_KEY = NULL unless joined separately.
  -- To allow matching by BUILDING_NUMBER, produce rows where BUILDING_KEY is the BUILDING_NUMBER value (handled in outer join by matching onto BUILDING_NUMBER)
  SELECT
    BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_KEY,
    COUNT(*) AS addr_count
  FROM fclt_building_address
  WHERE BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY BUILDING_NUMBER
) fba ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY OR fba.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN (
  -- counts from fac_building_address matched by BUILDING_KEY (which is BUILDING_KEY in that table)
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    COUNT(*) AS addr_count
  FROM fac_building_address
  GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
) fcltba ON fcltba.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN (
  -- alternate address table: fac_building_address can also have BUILDING_KEY as BUILDING_NUMBER in some extracts;
  -- include aggregated by BUILDING_NUMBER to catch those matches
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_NUMBER_KEY,
    COUNT(*) AS addr_count
  FROM fac_building_address
  WHERE BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY

  -- Note: this subselect intentionally exposes BUILDING_KEY column from fac_building_address (kept same name),
  -- outer join matches it to buildings.BUILDING_NUMBER to capture addresses keyed by number instead of key.
) facba ON facba.BUILDING_NUMBER_KEY = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
buildings_address_counts.description: Count address records linked to each building by BUILDING_KEY and BUILDING_NUMBER. Produces one row per building key with counts by matching on BUILDING_KEY or BUILDING_NUMBER where address tables exist. If no address tables exist in schema chunk, this view will produce zero counts by joining only to available address-like columns (none here) resulting in zero.

materials_reserved_cohort.name: materials_reserved_cohort
materials_reserved_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- material identifier: use TIP_MATERIAL.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY as materials.material_id
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS material_id,

  -- course subject identifier: link via TIP_DETAIL.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY -> TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  -- then use TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED.SUBJECT_ID as materials.course_subject_id
  `tip_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS course_subject_id,

  -- reservation flag: TIP_DETAIL.IS_RESERVED is not present; the reservation concept here is from library reserve tables.
  -- Use library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY presence as reservation_flag (cast to 'Y'/'N').
  -- Carry the base column LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY through (we expose reservation_flag as derived presence per instructions
  -- but we must expose a column named reservation_flag. Since no exact stored column exists, we expose a boolean-like flag derived
  -- from the join presence. This keeps material row-level grain and ties to original keys.)
  CASE WHEN `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS reservation_flag,

  -- reservation_status: use TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS (status value) as materials.reservation_status
  `tip_material_status`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS reservation_status

FROM `tip_material`
  -- join TIP_DETAIL to get relation between material and subject offered; TIP_DETAIL.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY -> TIP_MATERIAL.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  LEFT JOIN `tip_detail`
    ON `tip_detail`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`

  -- join TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED to get the SUBJECT_ID (course_subject_id)
  LEFT JOIN `tip_subject_offered`
    ON `tip_subject_offered`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `tip_detail`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`

  -- join TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS to get the status text
  LEFT JOIN `tip_material_status`
    ON `tip_material_status`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `tip_detail`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`

  -- left join library_reserve_matrl_detail to detect reserved materials (case-insensitive 'reserved' marker is not a column here;
  -- presence in library_reserve_matrl_detail indicates a reserve). Link by TIP_MATERIAL_KEY via LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY relation is not direct,
  -- but library_reserve_matrl_detail has LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY; we can match by TERM_CODE + SUBJECT_ID + (no direct material key).
  -- However to keep one row per material and to mark reservation, attempt to match by TIP_DETAIL.TERM_CODE and TIP_DETAIL.SUBJECT_ID
  -- to library_reserve_matrl_detail TERM_CODE and SUBJECT_ID. Use LEFT JOIN so non-reserved materials remain.
  LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`TERM_CODE` = `tip_detail`.`TERM_CODE`
   AND `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `tip_detail`.`SUBJECT_ID`

semantic_filters.reservation_flag_or_status: rows where reservation_flag indicates reserved OR reservation_status text equals 'reserved' (case-insensitive)

materials_reserved_cohort.description: Row-level cohort of material records that are marked as reserved (case-insensitive), exposing identifiers that link materials to course subject IDs and the material status value. Keeps one row per material record.

reserved_materials_title_length_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary key / grain
  lrmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS reserved_material_id,

  -- publication year pulled from library_reserve_catalog to match required source
  lrc.`CATALOG_YEAR` AS publication_year,

  -- title from library_reserve_catalog (keep NULLs as NULL)
  lrc.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS title,

  -- status from library_material_status joined via library_reserve_matrl_detail

  -- course identifier: use library_reserve_matrl_detail.SUBJECT_ID to represent course_id (keeps source column)
  lrmd.`SUBJECT_ID` AS course_id,

  -- repeat title as requested (same exact source as above)
  lrc.`CATALOG_TITLE` AS title_dup
FROM
  -- base detail that links reserve catalog entries to subjects/status
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lrmd
  LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog` lrc
    ON lrmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = lrc.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` lms
    ON lrmd.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`

iap_fee_values_per_person.name: iap_fee_values_per_person
iap_fee_values_per_person.body_sql:
SELECT
  dcc.SECTION_ID                            AS SECTION_ID,
  dcc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID           AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  dcc.SO_CLUSTER_TYPE                       AS SO_CLUSTER_TYPE,
  dcc.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE                   AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  -- attempt to extract a numeric fee value from common fee-like text fields in drupal_course_catalog
  -- look for patterns like "$123", "USD 123", or just digits; NULL if unparsable
  CAST(
    NULLIF(
      -- priority: explicit $amount (with optional commas), then "USD" prefix, then bare numbers
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        COALESCE(
          -- possible fee-like columns that might contain fee text; keep original sourcing from drupal_course_catalog
          -- (we do not invent columns from other tables)
          dcc.FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
          dcc.SPRING_INSTRUCTORS,
          dcc.STATUS_CHANGE,
          dcc.SUBJECT_DESCRIPTION,
          dcc.SUBJECT_TITLE,
          dcc.SUBJECT_SHORT_TITLE,
          dcc.LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE,
          dcc.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR
        , '')
      , '.*?\\$\\s*([0-9]{1,3}(?:,[0-9]{3})*(?:\\.[0-9]+)?).*', '\\1')
      , ''
    ) AS DECIMAL(12,2)
  ) AS fee_value
FROM drupal_course_catalog dcc
WHERE dcc.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND dcc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
iap_fee_values_per_person.description: Denormalized rows tying a person (MIT_ID) to an IAP category (SO_CLUSTER_TYPE) and a fee value extracted from any fee-like text columns present in course/section records. One row per person-section occurrence with parsed numeric fee_value (NULL if unparsable).

buildings_row_level_199.name: buildings_row_level_199
buildings_row_level_199.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME` AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  CASE
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) = '' THEN NULL
    -- if it's already an integer type, pass through
    WHEN JSON_VALID(JSON_QUOTE(CAST(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS CHAR))) AND `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS SIGNED)
    -- handle numeric-looking strings (allow leading/trailing spaces already trimmed)
    WHEN `buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*-?[0-9]+[[:space:]]*$' THEN CAST(TRIM(`buildings`.`BUILDING_COUNTER`) AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS `BUILDING_COUNTER`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`
FROM `buildings`
buildings_row_level_199.description: One canonical row per building, with BUILDING_COUNTER cleaned to a numeric integer when possible and NULL otherwise. Keeps primary building identifiers and attributes for downstream filtering/aggregation.

buildings_counter_stats.name: buildings_counter_stats
buildings_counter_stats.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- per-row helper: is this row's counter equal to the global max (1/0)
  CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER = (SELECT MAX(bb.BUILDING_COUNTER) FROM buildings bb WHERE bb.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS IS_GLOBAL_MAX,
  -- per-row helper: rank of this building_counter (1 = highest); ties get same rank
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY b.BUILDING_COUNTER DESC) AS BUILDING_COUNTER_RANK,
  -- per-row helper: dense rank for top-k without gaps
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY b.BUILDING_COUNTER DESC) AS BUILDING_COUNTER_DENSE_RANK,
  -- global aggregates carried through for convenience
  (SELECT MAX(bb.BUILDING_COUNTER) FROM buildings bb WHERE bb.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL) AS GLOBAL_MAX_BUILDING_COUNTER,
  (SELECT AVG(bb.BUILDING_COUNTER) FROM buildings bb WHERE bb.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL) AS GLOBAL_AVG_BUILDING_COUNTER,
  (SELECT STDDEV(bb.BUILDING_COUNTER) FROM buildings bb WHERE bb.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL) AS GLOBAL_STDDEV_BUILDING_COUNTER,
  (SELECT VARIANCE(bb.BUILDING_COUNTER) FROM buildings bb WHERE bb.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL) AS GLOBAL_VARIANCE_BUILDING_COUNTER,
  -- include warehouse load date from buildings for freshness/partitioning uses
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
FROM buildings b
WHERE b.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NOT NULL
buildings_counter_stats.description: Aggregate stats of BUILDING_COUNTER across all buildings (only numeric counts). Produces per-building max comparison helpers and global max counter value. Useful for top-k / tie queries on BUILDING_COUNTER.

students_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`MIT_ID`          AS `MIT_ID`,
  NULLIF(TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`FIRST_NAME`), '') AS `FIRST_NAME`,
  NULLIF(TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME`), '') AS `MIDDLE_NAME`,
  NULLIF(TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME`), '')  AS `LAST_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`HR_ORG_UNIT_ID` AS `HR_ORG_UNIT_ID`,
  -- canonical_full_name: first + (if middle present then ' ' + middle) + ' ' + last
  TRIM(
    CONCAT(
      COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`FIRST_NAME`), ''), ''),
      CASE WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME`), '') IS NOT NULL
           THEN CONCAT(' ', TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`MIDDLE_NAME`))
           ELSE ''
      END,
      CASE WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME`), '') IS NOT NULL
           THEN CONCAT(' ', TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME`))
           ELSE ''
      END
    )
  ) AS `canonical_full_name`
FROM
  `drupal_employee_directory`
WHERE
  NOT (
    ( `drupal_employee_directory`.`FIRST_NAME` IS NULL OR TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`FIRST_NAME`) = '' )
    AND
    ( `drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME` IS NULL OR TRIM(`drupal_employee_directory`.`LAST_NAME`) = '' )
  )
